As of v0.11.2, the prebuilds link the C++ standard library statically, so they no longer list `libc++_shared.so` among their needed libraries. As of v0.9.3, they also no longer list `libnativehelper.so`.

The addon finds its Java helper classes (`to.holepunch.bare.bluetooth.*`) by name through JNI, which R8 can't see when it shrinks an app. As of v0.11.7, the classes JAR embeds a keep rule for them (`bare-bluetooth-android.pro`), so R8 applies it to an app that depends on that JAR. With an earlier version, a release build that shrinks the app needs `-keep class to.holepunch.bare.bluetooth.** { *; }` in its own R8 rules.

from: #### `new BluetoothError(msg: string, fn?: Function, code?: string)`
to:
The package root exports `BluetoothError` as of v0.11.3. Earlier versions did not export the class from the package root, although the errors they raised were instances of it.

Failures reach your code three ways. A call can throw when the Android call itself fails, with the Java exception in the message, for example `java.lang.IllegalStateException: BT Adapter is not turned ON`. An operation that fails after the call went through is emitted as an `'error'` event carrying a `BluetoothError`. A failed write on an [`L2CAPChannel`](#l2capchannel) destroys the stream, so listen for `'error'` on the channel.

A duplex stream representing an L2CAP connection-oriented channel. Extends `Duplex` from \<https://github.com/holepunchto/bare-stream>. Typically obtained via the `'channelOpen'` event rather than constructed directly.

A failed write does not throw from `write()`. As of v0.11.1 it destroys the stream with the Java exception, for example `java.io.IOException: Broken pipe` once the peer is gone, so listen for `'error'` on the channel. An unhandled `'error'` still throws. A native channel error destroys the stream with that error, and a native close destroys it, instead of either being emitted directly.

to:
Open the GATT server. Call it once `state` is `'on'`; it throws unless the adapter is on, and it throws `GATT server already open` when the server is already open. The GATT server does not survive the adapter turning off, so on every transition back to `'on'` call `close()` and then `open()` again. Services do not survive a reopen and have to be added again. Added in v0.11.0.

`startAdvertising()` and `publishChannel()` do not check whether the GATT server is open.
